title: Snug and the Sneezy Dragon
markdown:
Snug the little goblin loved his home high in the Pebblecloud Peaks, where the air carried warm cedar and damp earth. Today his small feet padded the mellow cedar trail. Tall whispering trees wove a leafy roof. Sunlight fell like a thousand tiny golden coins on moss. His tummy rumbled, not from hunger, from a happy feeling that made his fuzzy green ears wiggle. He was on a very important mission: the most beautiful smoothest pebbles for his special collection, and for his grandmother, who was visiting tomorrow.

A whisper of worry rustled in him, dry leaves in the heart. Knees a little wobbly. Fuzzy tail tucked tight. What if a twig snapped too loudly? What if a shadow looked like something startling? Snug was not always the bravest goblin. Even a flitting butterfly could make him jump. He still wanted the prettiest stones. He shuffled on, bright curious eyes scanning for glints of colour and perfect shapes.

The path seemed ordinary. Sparkly quartz hid. River stones were all a bit too grey. He peeked behind a particularly large mossy boulder, cool and soft under his fingers. Cedars grew closer here, trunks like ancient silent guardians. This part of the trail felt a little unfamiliar, a little more quiet, as if the trees were holding their breath. A gentle tug from the unknown pulled him onward. He stepped off the main path onto a narrow track carpeted with emerald moss. He almost turned back, heart fluttering like a trapped bird, but the thought of his grandmother’s smile gave him courage.

Then: a bubbly sound, a tiny waterfall clearing its throat, a puff. Ah-CHOO! Shimmering smoke. Tiny bright orange twinkles dancing in the dappled light. A minuscule dragon tumbled from behind a cluster of moon-lilies. Scales like a rainbow after rain. Wide innocent eyes, wobbly, unsure. Ah-CHOO! Twinkles landed in a puddle and fizzed like lemonade.

Pip sat there, more confused than fearsome, tail thumping the moss, damp and bewildered by his own bursts of fire and fizz.

Snug’s first instinct was to jump, ears straight up, hands to his chest. Pip only looked surprised. Snug remembered wanting to be brave not only for pebbles. He breathed pine and secrets. A sparkly sneeze, still a sneeze. One small step, then another, silent on moss.

“Hello there,” he whispered.

Pip blinked, head tilt. Ah-CHOO! Twinkles fizzed near Snug’s toes. A shiver, then a strange calm. He stayed.

Pip whimpered, hiccupy, trying not to sneeze, nose wiggling with effort. Twinkles came from the sniffing. The moon-lilies beside them wore the fluffiest tickliest white fluff, drifting like dandelion seed.

“I think,” Snug said slowly, “the fluffy moon-lily fluff is tickling your nose.”

Pip looked at the lilies, at Snug, sniffed. Ah-CHOO! Snug gathered velvety fern leaves, cool and smooth. “Maybe these will feel better than the fluff.” Pip hesitated, tensed, leaned, sniffed.

Nose wiggled. No sneeze. A bolder sniff. A tiny happy sigh of warm air. The fern was not tickly at all.

Snug’s smile arrived like sunshine. Pip nudged his hand, scales warm. Snug stroked the smooth back, a living pearl breathing. Then he looked at his collection. Among the stones lay his most prized: a smooth grey pebble with one perfect vein of shimmering quartz. His absolute favourite. Pip needed a stiller nose more than Snug needed a prize. He rolled it across the moss until it stopped before the twitching snout.

Pip nudged the pebble, sniffed the moss Snug offered. A tiny hiccup-sneeze, only a puff, no sparks. A happy squeak like a bell. Snug scooped him up. Pip fitted, claws gentle on the tunic, a warm weight. Courage hummed, more solid than any pebble.

With Pip nestled safely in his arms, breathing soft and regular, Snug turned back toward the familiar cedar trail. The sun began to dip, painting clouds in pink and sleepy orange, a gentle farewell to the day. Pip nestled closer, little snores like tiny puffs of warm air against Snug’s cheek. Snug’s own steps felt lighter now, more confident. The shadows no longer seemed startling. A rustle in the leaves nearby might once have made him jump. He smiled. Only the wind saying hello. A quiet strength settled deep.

As they ambled home, the moon peeked from behind a wispy cloud, soft and silver, laying a glow over the path. Snug hummed a sleepy goblin lullaby his mother used to sing, as soothing as rustling leaves. Pip’s snores grew a little deeper. Snug nestled him into a soft mossy nook near the cozy doorstep, a perfect little bed, and watched the tiny chest rise and fall. A warm wave of contentment washed over him, like a gentle tide. Moonbeams painted silver stripes across the sleeping dragon. Soon the only sound was the breath of dreams beginning to unfurl, and the quartz pebble, still with Pip, doing a braver job than it had ever done in a collection.
